abstract: Post-translational modifications (PTMs) regulate protein activity and treatment-associated signalling, providing functional information that can connect drug-response estimates with candidate pharmacodynamic measurements. Assessing this information requires a framework that determines its contribution beyond fixed molecular features while retaining the identity of the modified sites underlying model predictions. We developed the PTM Biological Dynamics Layer (PTM-BDL), which integrates typed PTM states with protein sequence, structure-derived and drug chemical features to predict log-transformed half-maximal inhibitory concentration and resistance while providing site-level interpretation through integrated gradients. Retrospective evaluation used source-derived and propagated PTM profiles across biologically distinct BCR-ABL, HDAC/EP300 and EGFR/ERBB2 settings, yielding internal areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROCs) between 0.785 and 0.946. Retraining demonstrated a consistent incremental contribution from PTM inputs in K562/CML, with a mean AUROC increase of 0.0268 and positive gains in all five folds, alongside more modest incremental gains in HeLa/HDAC and EGFR/ERBB2. Within K562/CML, CRKL Y207 and STAT5A Y694 retained the leading attribution ranks for their proteins across three seeds, while greater PTM attribution in dasatinib than in cytotoxic drug contexts identified a focused setting for pharmacodynamic investigation. These findings support context-dependent use of PTM information and connect predictive assessment with prioritisation of individual sites, providing a basis for targeted pharmacodynamic measurements and independent experimental validation.
